https://w3id.org/eudpp/textile-assessmen.notes: Advice MAP -> oec:testedConditions. The upstream property links an assessment execution to the condition under which it is performed, which aligns with our existing property oec:testedConditions that describes the conditions under which performance was tested.
Advice MAP -> eucpr:hasCharacteristicValue. Both properties relate a measurement result to its quantitative value; eucpr:hasCharacteristicValue already captures this relationship.

https://w3id.org/eudpp/textile-associate.notes: Advice MAP -> euelec:hasComponentType. The upstream property links a non‑textile component to its type concept, which is already represented by euelec:hasComponentType in our vocabulary.
Advice MAP -> eutex:chemicalPurpose. The upstream property describes the functional role of a textile chemical substance, which is already represented by eutex:chemicalPurpose in our vocabulary.

https://w3id.org/eudpp/textile-connector.notes: Advice MAP -> oec:SingleValuedDataElement. The upstream class represents a numerical value with unit, which is already captured by oec:SingleValuedDataElement in our vocabulary.

https://w3id.org/eudpp/textile-context#h.notes: Advice MAP -> eucpr:hasCharacteristicValue. Both properties link a context observation to a quantitative value; eucpr:hasCharacteristicValue is the existing DPP term that captures this relationship.

https://w3id.org/eudpp/textile-core#Reus.notes: Advice OUT_OF_SCOPE. The upstream class represents a product type that is explicitly excluded from the DPP scope, so it does not need to be modeled in the vocabulary.

https://w3id.org/eudpp/textile-core#hasF.notes: Advice MAP -> oec:massFraction. The upstream property describes the mass fraction of a fibre component, which is directly represented by our existing term oec:massFraction.

https://w3id.org/eudpp/textile-core#hasT.notes: Advice MAP -> oec:massFraction. The upstream property describes the mass fraction of textile fibres, which is directly represented by our existing term oec:massFraction.

https://w3id.org/eudpp/textile-core#jrcE.notes: Advice MAP -> eudr:exemptionReasonCode. The upstream property captures a coded reason for excluding a textile product class from the JRC study scope, which is functionally equivalent to an exemption reason code in our vocabulary.

https://w3id.org/eudpp/textile-durabilit.notes: Advice MAP -> eutex:hasDurabilityInfo. The upstream property ‘has durability aspect’ directly corresponds to the existing DPP class property eutex:hasDurabilityInfo, which links a textile product to its durability metrics.

Advice MAP -> eutex:hasDurabilityInfo. The upstream property ‘has observed performance parameter’ is effectively covered by the existing DPP property eutex:hasDurabilityInfo, which links a textile product to its durability metrics and observed performance data.

https://w3id.org/eudpp/textile-indicator.notes: Advice MAP -> oec:stageValue. The upstream property links an Indicator to a generic quantitative value, which is functionally equivalent to our oec:stageValue that represents an indicator’s quantitative value for a lifecycle module.

https://w3id.org/eudpp/textile-process#D.notes: Advice MAP -> eubat:TemperatureRange. The upstream term represents a temperature parameter for dyeing, which aligns with the existing TemperatureRange class in our vocabulary; no new term is required.

https://w3id.org/eudpp/textile-process#T.notes: Advice MAP -> eubat:TemperatureRange. The upstream concept of Temperature control is effectively the same as the existing eubat:TemperatureRange, which captures a temperature range specification for an operating context.
Advice CARRIER -> EPCIS event. A concrete occurrence of a textile process is naturally represented by an EPCIS event, which already captures the execution details within the DPP data exchange.

https://w3id.org/eudpp/textile-process#U.notes: Advice CARRIER -> CBV bizStep use. The ‘Use or wear process’ is a lifecycle stage that can be represented by the existing CBV bizStep ‘use’, which already captures use‑phase events in EPCIS.

https://w3id.org/eudpp/textile-process#h.notes: Advice MAP -> eutex:hasCareInstructions. The upstream property ‘has care instruction’ is equivalent to the existing eutex:hasCareInstructions, which already captures product‑specific care instructions.

Advice MAP -> eucpr:hasCharacteristicValue. The upstream property links a process parameter setting to a quantitative value, which is conceptually equivalent to the existing eucpr:hasCharacteristicValue property that associates a quantitative value with an essential characteristic.

https://w3id.org/eudpp/textile-process#i.notes: Advice CARRIER -> EPCIS productEvent. The upstream property simply links a textile process execution to the EPCIS product event that records it, which is already represented by the standard EPCIS productEvent construct.

https://w3id.org/eudpp/textile-process#r.notes: Advice CARRIER -> EPCIS productEvent. The upstream property simply links a product event to the textile process execution it records, which is already represented by the standard EPCIS productEvent construct.

https://w3id.org/eudpp/textile-process#u.notes: Advice MAP -> eutex:chemicalPurpose. The upstream property ‘uses chemical function’ aligns with the existing DPP term eutex:chemicalPurpose, which captures the technical purpose of a chemical in textile processes.

Advice MAP -> eutex:hasTextileChemicals. The upstream property ‘uses chemical substance’ describes chemicals employed in a textile process, which is effectively the same concept as eutex:hasTextileChemicals – chemicals used in textile production.

https://w3id.org/eudpp/textile-recyclabi.notes: Advice MAP -> eutex:RecyclabilityAssessment. The upstream Recyclability class matches the existing eutex:RecyclabilityAssessment, which captures a product’s potential for recycling under specified contexts.

Advice CARRIER -> EPCIS event with CBV bizStep recycling. The concept represents a specific type of EPCIS event; it is already covered by the generic EPCIS event construct with an appropriate bizStep.

Advice CARRIER -> EPCIS event with CBV bizStep recycling. The concept represents a specific type of EPCIS event; it is already covered by the generic EPCIS event construct with an appropriate bizStep.
Advice CARRIER -> EPCIS event with CBV bizStep recycling. The concept is an occurrence of textile recycling, which is already represented by a generic EPCIS event with the appropriate bizStep.

Advice MAP -> eutex:hasSortingFactors. The upstream property ‘applies sorting criterion’ is conceptually equivalent to the existing eutex:hasSortingFactors, which captures sorting factors used in recycling processes.

Advice MAP -> eutex:hasRecyclabilityAssessment. The upstream property ‘assesses recyclability of’ directly corresponds to the existing eutex:hasRecyclabilityAssessment, which links a textile product to its recyclability assessment.

Advice MAP -> euelec:hasMaterialRecoveryResults. The property euelec:hasMaterialRecoveryResults captures the measured outcome of a textile recycling event, including recovered material outputs, matching the upstream hasRecoveredMaterial concept.

Advice MAP -> eutex:hasRecyclabilityAssessment. The upstream property hasRecyclabilityAspect corresponds to the existing eutex:hasRecyclabilityAssessment, which links a product to its recyclability assessment.

Advice MAP -> oec:recyclabilityScore. The upstream hasRecyclabilityScore directly corresponds to the existing oec:recyclabilityScore property, which captures a numeric recyclability score for a product.

Advice MAP -> eutex:hasWasteOriginType. The upstream concept of a waste source type (lifecycle‑stage category where the textile became waste) aligns with our existing Waste Origin Type classification, so mapping is appropriate.

Advice MAP -> euelec:recyclingProcess. The upstream property links a recycling route to its principal recycling process type, which matches the existing euelec:recyclingProcess property that describes the treatment or recycling process applied to an item.

https://w3id.org/eudpp/textile-repairabi.notes: Advice MAP -> oec:RepairabilityInfo. The upstream Repairability concept is equivalent to the existing oec:RepairabilityInfo class, which already represents repair and maintenance information per ESPR Article 7.
Advice MAP -> euelec:repairType. The upstream property describes the type of repair action performed, which aligns with our existing euelec:repairType that captures the kind of repair performed.

Advice MAP -> oec:hasRepairInstructions. The upstream property ‘has repair guidance’ is functionally equivalent to our existing oec:hasRepairInstructions, which links a product to repair instructions or manuals.

Advice MAP -> oec:hasSparePartsAvailability. The upstream ‘has spare‑part availability condition’ is functionally equivalent to our existing oec:hasSparePartsAvailability, which records the duration for which spare parts will be available.

Advice MAP -> oec:hasRepairProvider. The upstream ‘provided by’ property is functionally equivalent to our existing oec:hasRepairProvider, which links a product (or service) to one or more authorised repair providers.

Advice MAP -> oec:hasRepairInstructions. The upstream ‘provides guidance’ property is functionally equivalent to our existing oec:hasRepairInstructions, which links a repair service (or product) to the URL or reference of repair instructions and manuals.

https://w3id.org/eudpp/textile-structure.notes: Advice MAP -> eucpr:hasCharacteristicValue. The upstream property ‘has characteristic value’ is a generic quantitative link between a textile structure characteristic and its numeric value, which matches the existing eucpr:hasCharacteristicValue construct.
